description: createApiKey accepts a non-null harnessId (data.harnessId) and inserts without any try/catch, so calling it with a harnessId whose (userId,orgId,harnessId) triple already has an active row raises a raw Postgres 23505 from uq_api_keys_active_harness that is never mapped to the ApiKeyManagerError('CONFLICT') sentinel the harness methods produce, leaking a DB-level error to callers.
reason: Confirmed: createApiKey (lines 118-128) inserts harnessId (data.harnessId ?? null) with no try/catch, and the partial index uq_api_keys_active_harness (schema/api-keys.ts:89-91, WHERE revoked_at IS NULL) would raise an unmapped 23505 for a duplicate active triple — unlike createHarnessKeyIfNoneActive which wraps the insert and calls isActiveHarnessUniqueViolation; however no production caller drives a non-null harnessId through this generic method (POST /keys at auth-routes.ts:84-119 never sets harnessId; harness creation uses createHarnessKeyIfNoneActive), so it is a latent defensive gap exercised only by tests with unique harnessIds (test 2, line 138-143).
